episode_scope: The May 14–June 9, 2024 union wage strike; excludes later Faroese or Icelandic seafarer disputes.

status_basis.text: Local.fo explicitly reports the June 9 agreement immediately ended the strike.

outcomes.summary: Five unions and employers signed a two-year contract with a total hourly wage increase of DKK 16.80 over two years.

favours.actor: Workers covered by the five unions
favours.note: The higher contractual wage benefits covered workers; purchasing power and employment effects were not established.

research_note: Two reports from one local publisher; do not treat them as independent corroboration. End article page says June 10 although search metadata says June 9. AI-assisted; no human sign-off.

research_note: BBC article includes wire material and named official statements. No later outcome or protest cessation inferred. AI-assisted; no human sign-off.

episode_scope: The January 2024 roadblock mobilisation of FNSEA and Young Farmers through their February 1 suspension; excludes continued action by other unions and later farmer campaigns.

status_basis.text: RFI explicitly reports the two major unions suspended protests on February 1. This describes their suspension, not the end of all French farmer activism.

outcomes.summary: Government announced annual €150 million livestock support and a pause in the national pesticide reduction plan, among other concessions.

favours.actor: Farmers seeking immediate financial and regulatory relief
favours.note: The announcements meet some immediate union demands; implementation and longer-term income effects were not verified.

research_note: RFI article credits AFP; it is one reporting stream. Its February 2 update documents the suspension while noting other-union mobilisation. AI-assisted; no human sign-off.

favours.note: They kept one tax benefit and gained time on another, but the planned diesel phase-out remained.

episode_scope: The documented 2024 strike rounds from January 3 through September acceptance, within a dispute that began in 2022; excludes later resident-doctor disputes.

status_basis.text: BMA says acceptance ended the pay dispute; the government announced the accepted agreement on September 16.

outcomes.summary: Doctors accepted an agreement providing additional backdated pay uplifts and a 2024–25 increase of 6% plus £1,000.

favours.actor: Resident doctors covered by the England agreement
favours.note: Contractual pay rises benefit covered doctors; full restoration of historical purchasing power remained a wider BMA goal.

research_note: Union and government are primary negotiating parties with incentives to present the deal positively; BBC independently documents the January strike. Government publication date is September 16 despite Exa's previous-day metadata. AI-assisted; no human sign-off.

favours.note: They relinquished office politically; students' substantive accountability demands remained unmet, so no overall protest victory is inferred.

episode_scope: The January 22–30, 2024 general-education teachers' strike and related solidarity mobilisation; excludes later education disputes.

outcomes.summary: Union accepted €5.7 million additional pay funding, raising the minimum salary to €1,820, with further collective bargaining planned.

favours.note: They gained pay funding but accepted less than their initial demand; longer-term targets were commitments, not verified achievements.

research_note: ERR reporting and ministry's Estonian-language primary record corroborate onset and ending; parties had incentives to emphasize settlement. Tartu rally is identified in ERR's caption. AI-assisted; no human sign-off.
